# CLI reference

## help

JSON verbs for SessionStart and SessionEnd reason=compact hooks. CLI aliases: --help, -h.

### Parameters

_None._

### Result

- `verbs` ([]VerbSummary): Array of {name, description} for every verb in the manifest.

### Errors

_None._

## spawn

Launch a tracked agent in tmux. Returns the instance_id and pre_trust (ok, skipped or failed) right away; the row is pending from its insert until the agent reports in, then waiting. Creation bounded by the create timeout; timeout: ErrTmuxUnresponsive (UNAVAILABLE, transient): the session may have been created; the row stays pending; do not retry until get shows the row ended or missing, since a retry without an explicit id would start a second agent; then retry an explicit id with the reuse opt-in and the row's agent, which get shows. This store's session labelled by an explicit id but no row (left over from an earlier life): ErrTmuxSessionConflict; nothing is written. Name already held: spawn ends its new row at once (unless error says otherwise), returning ErrTmuxSessionConflict naming the holder's tmux id and whether its label names this id; ErrTmuxSessionCreate (LAUNCH FAILURE) if holder vanished first, ErrTmuxNotAvailable (ENVIRONMENT) or ErrTmuxUnresponsive if tmux cannot run/be read. ErrTmuxSessionConflict is CONFLICT (permanent until a human looks): another row's/another agent-director store's session is another agent; must not be ended; a leftover of an earlier life or a session with no valid instance id is a human's to end (see docs/operator-actions.md); then, if refused for a held name, spawn the id again with reuse_finished (--reuse-finished on the CLI) and the row's agent. ErrInternal, nothing created or changed: the collision pre-check could not read the store (id use unknown), or a reuse's archive of the previous session or its change failed (a busy store included), or a reused row's recorded name is unusable (see kill). To end a live row (pending included) and relaunch its id, follow the live-row sequence in kill's description.

### Parameters

- `cwd` (string, required): Absolute (or ~/-prefixed) path the Spawn's agent starts in. Required.
- `template` (string, optional): Optional named template under ~/.config/agent-director/templates/. Per-call params layer on top (scalars replace; maps merge; permissions arrays concat; agent_args replaces wholesale).
- `agent` (string, optional): The agent to launch: claude (Claude Code), codex (Codex) or cursor (Cursor fresh Linux ACP), case-sensitive; empty or absent means not given. A per-call agent overrides the template's; with neither, ErrAgentMissing; any other value, ErrAgentInvalid. A template's non-empty agent_args are inherited only when the template's agent is this agent, else ErrAgentArgsMismatch (this call's supplied agent_args replace them, including an explicit empty Go/MCP array; CLI/TypeScript empty arrays are omitted). A codex or cursor spawn with any allow, deny or ask entry, from the call or the template, is refused with ErrPermissionsUnsupported. The row records the agent for life; get and list show it.
- `instance_id` (string, optional): Optional explicit id; an empty or absent id mints a fresh UUID4. An explicit id containing an ASCII control character (0x00-0x1f or 0x7f) is rejected with ErrInvalidFlags. An explicit id that already has a row returns ErrInstanceIdCollision: without the reuse opt-in any existing row collides, in any state; with it, only a live row (pending included) or a row that changed or was removed after this spawn examined it.
- `label` ([]string, optional): Label k=v entries, one per array element (on the CLI, a repeatable flag). Each becomes AGENT_DIRECTOR_LABEL_<UPPER_KEY> on the session env and persists in labels.
- `allow` ([]string, optional): permissions.allow entries, one per array element (on the CLI, a repeatable flag), concatenated with the user / project tiers.
- `deny` ([]string, optional): permissions.deny entries, one per array element (on the CLI, a repeatable flag), concatenated with the user / project tiers.
- `ask` ([]string, optional): permissions.ask entries, one per array element (on the CLI, a repeatable flag), concatenated with the user / project tiers.
- `relay_mode` (string, optional): on / off. Empty falls back to config defaults.relay_mode (default off). Over MCP, a serve process from before the rename (0.10.x and earlier, or 0.11.0-rc.1, which counts as 0.11.0) knows this parameter only as relay-mode and silently ignores relay_mode.
- `extra_env` (map[string]string, optional): Env-var entries injected on the tmux session env, as an object mapping each variable name to its value (on the CLI, a repeatable KEY=VALUE flag). Keys rejected with ErrReservedEnvKey, a template's included, never rewritten: the reserved names AGENT_DIRECTOR_* and HOME with any value (an extra_env HOME would move the agent's hook to another agent-director store; set an absolute CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (Claude Code) or CODEX_HOME (Codex) to give the agent its own config), and a key that is not a valid env-var name (empty, or containing '=' or a NUL byte, which tmux would read as a different variable; the message says which); auth env vars (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN) allowed. Cursor: CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR and CURSOR_DATA_DIR must be nonempty absolute, lexically clean paths without control bytes; literal selection only, no expansion or filesystem validation. Directory selection uses existing personal login, without account isolation. Explicit CURSOR_API_KEY or AGENT_CLI_CREDENTIAL_STORE, even empty, is refused with ErrReservedEnvKey before mutation or launch because the credential profile is unreleased. Absent Cursor selectors are not inherited from caller, parent or server. Resume uses saved selection; reuse uses the new resolved request. Over MCP, a serve process from before the rename (0.10.x and earlier, or 0.11.0-rc.1, which counts as 0.11.0) knows this parameter only as extra-env and silently ignores extra_env, so its variables (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and CODEX_HOME included) are not set.
- `agent_args` ([]string, optional): Pass-through argv to the agent program, one argument per array element (on the CLI, the arguments after --). Claude refuses --settings, --output-format and print (-p/--print, clusters included). Session selectors/owned values are refused except on a finished-agent switch: dropped_args reports their removal; the agent starts fresh and resumes nothing. Exact denied long tokens owned as values always refuse. For a codex agent, refused (ErrSpawnDeniedFlag): a Codex subcommand in command position, --remote, --remote-auth-token-env, -c/--config keys at, above or under hooks, tui.disable_paste_burst or features.hooks, and --disable hooks; with disable_ask_user on, also --enable default_mode_request_user_input and the question-tool keys. agent-director adds no second --no-daemon, --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust (pre-trust ok) or --enable write_stdin_approval when the arguments already carry one before any --; Codex rejects a flag the arguments themselves repeat. Cursor accepts --model/-m (split or equals), --mode agent|plan|ask, --plan and one final initial prompt (use -- before a flag-like prompt). Explicit mode is configured through ACP before prompt admission; launch success alone does not confirm it. Other or malformed Cursor arguments return ErrSpawnDeniedFlag; remove the named argument and any owned value, then retry.
- `no_pre_trust` (bool, optional): Skip the folder pre-trust. For a claude agent, pre-trust pre-writes projects.<cwd>.hasTrustDialogAccepted=true into the spawn's .claude.json (resolves to <CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/.claude.json if CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is set in extra_env, otherwise ~/.claude.json). For a codex agent, it puts the cwd's trust and the hook-trust bypass on the launch's command line and writes no file, so Codex does not stop at its folder-trust prompt. Default off (best-effort pre-trust for Claude/Codex). Cursor grants no trust: failed by default (ACP pre-trust unsupported), skipped with no_pre_trust; permission policy is independent and readiness is not guaranteed. For all three agents, the choice is recorded on the row until the next spawn or reuse, and every resume follows it: no pre-trust is attempted over an opt-out. Over MCP, a serve process from before the fix (0.10.x and earlier, or 0.11.0-rc.1, which counts as 0.11.0) silently ignores this parameter under either spelling.
- `tmux_session_name` (string, optional): Optional explicit tmux session name. Empty/omitted falls back to <basename(cwd)>-<id[:8]>. Validated app-side: rejects empty (when supplied), '#' ':' '.' '$' '\' (backslash), ASCII control chars, non-UTF-8, and >64 bytes. NO DB uniqueness check; a name already held by a tmux session when spawn creates its session ends the new row at once and returns the classified error spawn's description states (ErrTmuxSessionConflict naming the holding session), unless spawn refused earlier and wrote nothing. Name reuse across ended spawns is supported. Over MCP, a serve process from before the fix (0.10.x and earlier, or 0.11.0-rc.1, which counts as 0.11.0) silently ignores this parameter under either spelling.
- `reuse_finished` (bool, optional): Opt in to reusing an explicit instance_id whose row is finished (ended or missing): the id starts again on that row. A live row (pending included) still collides with ErrInstanceIdCollision, as does a row that changed or was removed after this spawn examined it; nothing is changed then. No effect without an explicit instance_id (a minted id cannot collide). Applies to this call only; no template or config setting carries it. The default (off) is unchanged: any existing row with the id collides. With no dropped arguments, a successful spawn does not say whether it created a fresh row or reset a finished one. Nonempty dropped_args identifies reuse that switches a finished row's agent; the CLI prints a notice when arguments are dropped. The spawn names its agent (agent, or the template's) and the reused row takes it: to reuse a row for the agent it ran, pass the row's agent, which get shows. Only an agent switch starts a new life; same-agent reuse keeps session history and subagent records but starts a fresh conversation. A switch back also starts with no memory of its earlier lives: resume and get never use or show an earlier life's history. Resume continues only the latest session; older sessions remain listed for inspection only. AD-agent children keep their parent_id; the append-only trail retains earlier lives. Cursor subagent tracking remains unsupported (tracked=false, empty records). A failed launch conditionally restores the prior row, agent, life and history only while the reset row is unchanged; a create timeout or lost reply never restores. Requests deleted and subagents closed by the reset are not revived. Retrying a failed plain spawn: after a held-name refusal (duplicate session) the row is already ended unless the error says otherwise, so the retry's lookup decides it at once; after any other failed launch the row stays pending and an opted-in retry collides until find-missing marks it missing, which happens only after the pending grace period (60 s by default). Feature detection: read the version of the binary that serves the caller: on the CLI the version verb; over MCP the version tool, which reports the running serve process's version until that process restarts; in the TypeScript client binaryVersion (from Client.create() or resolveSystemBinary()), never version(), which is the npm package's version. A release candidate X.Y.Z-rc.N counts as X.Y.Z. A build without a release stamp reports 0.0.0-dev (a make build) or dev (a plain go build); a caller cannot compare it and relies on the older-binary behaviour: an older binary returns ErrInvalidFlags on the CLI and in the TypeScript client, and over MCP silently ignores the parameter, so a finished row gives ErrInstanceIdCollision. Over MCP, a serve process from before the rename (0.10.x and earlier, or 0.11.0-rc.1, which counts as 0.11.0 and knows this parameter only as reuse-finished) silently ignores reuse_finished, so a finished row gives ErrInstanceIdCollision. Use it as the same user and in the same tmux environment as the agents. So kill's success on a finished row is not verification of exit; on the wrong tmux server, a row wrongly marked missing, kill's no-op success and a reuse together start a second agent for the same id.

### Result

- `instance_id` (string): The id (caller-supplied or freshly-minted UUID4) the row is tracked under.
- `pre_trust` (string): What the launch's folder-trust pre-trust did. Cursor: no trust grant, failed by default or skipped with no_pre_trust; never ok. For Claude/Codex: ok = the folder trust took effect (claude: the entry was written to .claude.json; codex: the launch carries the folder trust and the hook-trust bypass); skipped = pre-trust was off for this launch because the caller passed no_pre_trust, so nothing was attempted; failed = pre-trust was attempted and the entry was not written (for a claude agent, the .claude.json file is missing, or could not be read, parsed or written, or extra_env sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to a path that is not absolute; for a codex agent, extra_env sets CODEX_HOME to a path that is not absolute, and the launch carries neither the folder trust nor the hook-trust bypass); the launch still proceeds and the agent may stop at its folder-trust prompt (Claude Code's or Codex's).
- `dropped_args` ([]string): Original resume arguments removed on a finished-agent switch, in argv order. Omitted when empty; starts fresh and resumes nothing.

## status

Row state: pending/waiting/working/ask_user/check_permission/ended/missing/stuck. stuck: unanswered permission fallback. pending: launch (spawn/reuse/resume) underway; no SessionStart hook report yet; may be loading or at a startup prompt. Resumed pending keeps session id/history.

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the Spawn to inspect.

### Result

- `state` (string): Current state, one of the allowed values. pending: a launch (spawn, reuse or resume) is in progress and the agent has not reported in yet (its SessionStart hook); it may be loading or waiting at a startup prompt. A resumed pending row keeps its session id and history (non-empty session_id). `missing` is the sweep's judgement on the evidence available to it, not proof that the agent has exited. With [state] settle_ms set in config.toml (whole milliseconds from 0 to 60000, 0 or unset is off; a value outside that range is refused, never capped), state is the settled state: a state a hook wrote shows only once it has held that long, and the last settled state shows meanwhile, so a change that reverts sooner never shows; ended, missing and a state a command wrote (spawn, resume, find-missing) show at once. Nothing marks a state as late, and the setting covers every caller on the host. A turn shorter than settle_ms never shows (a waiting agent that replies sooner reads waiting throughout), so keep it at 1000 to 2000. Except for independently settled family_state, the row's other fields, and the verbs that act on it (send-keys, decide, pause, resume, kill, find-missing, expire, spawn), follow its live state, which can be newer: a refusal can name a state status does not show yet.
- `context` (object): Experimental context estimate: agent internals and this output shape have no stable-format guarantee. Always an object with used_tokens (integer?), window_tokens (integer?), fraction (number?; used_tokens divided by window_tokens), source (string?) and as_of (RFC3339 UTC timestamp with millisecond precision?). Unknown retains all five keys with null values. Readings estimate last-response occupancy, never cumulative billing. Claude 2.1.280 first-party pairs automatically composed capacity callbacks with on-demand transcript usage for the same resolved model, response and current live writer, without provider, endpoint or window overrides. Codex 0.159.2 OpenAI requires admitted fresh-startup provenance and a current live writer; existing, resumed or unproven sessions return unknown. Its sequential rollouts pair last_token_usage.total_tokens with the same session's reported usable model_context_window; source codex_jsonl_last_token_usage. as_of is the source measurement time, never read time. Claude and Codex usage is read on demand without a usage cache or wall-clock age cutoff; stored capacity metadata is not cached usage. Missing, malformed, incomplete, unsupported or unresolvable evidence yields unknown; compaction requires later valid usage. Both Cursor versions have successful native interactive captures. Managed ACP lacks the ordinary usage-bearing afterAgentResponse/stop path, exposes only stopReason in prompt results and exposes no manual /summarize command. Both versions have a native shared-resource preCompact executor path; automatic managed delivery remains unqualified. Cursor context is unknown in this build; numeric support is deferred until upstream ACP supplies usage.
- `family_state` (string): Complete stored family (self and live descendants at every depth, including through retained ended/missing intermediates). Uses stored raw member states: waiting exactly when every live member is waiting, or no live members remain; otherwise working. With [state] settle_ms, both directions settle once from the aggregate change, independently of state and depth. New/upgraded families start raw; later timing survives reopening. List filters and limits do not restrict family membership. Reporting never waits; waiting does not establish readiness, action safety or task success. Permissions remain per agent.
- `stuck_reason` (string?): Present only while displayed stuck. stuck with stuck_reason permission_unanswered reports a current unanswered, unproven fallen-back request on Claude, Codex or Cursor after [state] permission_unanswered_timeout_seconds (whole seconds, default/zero 30, range 1 to 9223372036), measured from its established fallback, followed by ordinary settling detected on reads. Independent requests remain eligible; detail selects earliest fallback, then lexical request token. since is the successful read that committed displayed entry, in RFC3339 UTC with exactly millisecond precision. Clearing retains displayed detail through settlement; representative changes preserve since. Observation writes never wait and skipped samples retain the committed display. This is report-only: raw command guards and dialog holds remain authoritative; live stuck members contribute working to family_state. No background observation is added.
- `since` (string?): Actual committed displayed stuck entry, RFC3339 UTC with exactly millisecond precision; omitted otherwise. Retained while clearing settles and when representative request changes.
- `request_token` (string?): Selected qualifying permission request token; only while displayed permission_unanswered. Earliest fallback, then ascending lexical token.
- `tool_name` (string?): Selected qualifying request's tool name; only while displayed permission_unanswered.
- `tmux_session_name` (string?): Attach target; present only while displayed stuck.
- `launch_started_at` (timestamp?): Start of the launch in progress: RFC3339 UTC with millisecond precision. Present only while the row is pending; omitted otherwise. It follows the row's live state: with [state] settle_ms set, a row whose agent has reported in can read pending without it for up to settle_ms.

### Errors

- `ErrSpawnNotFound`

- `stuck_reason` (string?): Present only while displayed stuck. stuck with stuck_reason permission_unanswered reports a current unanswered, unproven fallen-back request on Claude, Codex or Cursor after [state] permission_unanswered_timeout_seconds (whole seconds, default/zero 30, range 1 to 9223372036), measured from its established fallback, followed by ordinary settling detected on reads. Clearing retains displayed detail through settlement; representative changes preserve since. Observation writes never wait and skipped samples retain the committed display.
