- `since` (string?): Actual committed displayed stuck entry, RFC3339 UTC with exactly millisecond precision; omitted otherwise. Retained while clearing settles and when representative request changes.
- `request_token` (string?): Selected qualifying permission request token; only while displayed permission_unanswered. Earliest fallback, then ascending lexical token.
- `tool_name` (string?): Selected qualifying request's tool name; only while displayed permission_unanswered.
- `cwd` (string): Canonicalized cwd.
- `agent` (string): The agent the row runs: claude (Claude Code), codex (Codex) or cursor (Cursor). Set at spawn, replaced by a reuse, followed by resume.
- `tmux_session_name` (string): tmux session under which the Spawn is running.
- `tmux_socket` (string?): The tmux socket the row's launch uses; omitted when the row has no recorded socket.
- `agent_args` ([]string): Verbatim argv passed through to the agent program.
- `relay_mode` (string): on / off.
- `jsonl_path` (string): Current session's transcript path, persisted by the hooks; legacy rows may be empty. Resume tries this path, then for claude recomputes the current session's path from cwd + session_id (under a usable absolute CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR from extra_env, otherwise ~/.claude). A codex row uses only its recorded path; resume never builds one for it. Older sessions are never candidates.
- `session_id` (string): Agent session id, recorded from the agent's hooks: Claude's is its transcript file's name, Codex's the session_id its hooks report. Empty until the first SessionStart.
- `labels` (map[string]string): Caller-supplied labels.
- `started_at` (timestamp): Row insert time.
- `last_seen_at` (timestamp): Last hook UPSERT time.
- `ended_at` (timestamp?): Set when state moves to ended (omitted while live).
- `launch_started_at` (timestamp?): Start of the launch in progress: RFC3339 UTC with millisecond precision. Present only while the row is pending; omitted otherwise. It follows the row's live state: with [state] settle_ms set, a row whose agent has reported in can read pending without it for up to settle_ms.
- `liveness_unverified_since` (timestamp?): RFC3339 timestamp of the first sweep that noted this live row (left it unverified, or noted it unreported); kept while later sweeps change liveness_note, unreported included. Cleared to NULL together with liveness_note when a sweep finds the agent process alive, except on a pending row it notes unreported and a pending row noted provenance_conflict, which keeps it; null/omitted while the row has no note.
- `liveness_note` (string?): Reason token of the latest sweep that left this live row unverified (its agent process could not be checked and tmux did not settle it), for example process_not_seen_session_present, process_not_seen_tmux_unchecked, probe_eacces, tmux_server_changed or provenance_conflict; overwritten when the reason changes. Cleared to NULL together with liveness_unverified_since when a sweep finds the agent process alive, except on a pending row it notes unreported and a pending row noted provenance_conflict, which keeps it; null/omitted while the row has no note. Or unreported, on a pending row past the pending grace period: its agent is alive, but no hook has reported since its launch, so it may sit at an agent startup screen or idle at its prompt. The row stays pending. To act on it: read-pane, then send-keys with allow_pending (--allow-pending on the CLI); only a caller that looked should type. A later sweep that finds the agent alive keeps the note; the agent's next hook clears it. unreported never replaces provenance_conflict.
- `permission_requests` ([]object): Open permission requests: those that still await an answer (not acked by their relay hook and not answered at the pane, decided or not; a request with no recorded settle instant while undecided). Always a non-null array ([] when empty). Populated only when the row's live state is check_permission; empty array for all other states (a row can read waiting, working or ask_user while a request is still open: follow a tracked request with get-permission). Requests are never delayed by [state] settle_ms, so with it set a row can also read any state (even ended or missing) with open requests listed, or check_permission with [], for up to settle_ms. Each element: request_id (int) — autoincrement row id; request_token (string) — UUIDv4 request token, pass to decide verb to target this row; tool_name (string) — the supplied tool name or Cursor action title/plan name; tool_input (string) — raw JSON string of the tool's input, NOT a nested object (consumers parse it themselves). Cursor preserves the received permission/plan params envelope byte for byte, including options and absent/null fields, without adding internal context; requested_at (RFC3339 timestamp) — when the request was recorded; decision and decision_reason (string?) — the recorded verdict, not the outcome; and the delivery facts as get-permission returns them: delivery (delivered, not_confirmed or fallen_back), confirm_by (timestamp), hook_alive (bool?), hook_gone_at (timestamp?), attempted_decision (string?), attempted_at (timestamp?), tool_use_id (string?), pane_answer (none or intent on an open request), pane_as (string?), proven_gone_at (timestamp?), proven_gone_how (string?) and unproven_since (timestamp?). get and list never wait for the store's write lock.
- `unproven_requests` ([]object): Every permission request of the row that the agent has not proven gone (proven_gone_at null), oldest first, in any state but ended and missing ([] on those). Unlike permission_requests it also lists requests agent-director's records read closed (delivered, answered at the pane, or recorded answered outside it), each with unproven_since: a request that stays unproven a while after it is a reason to read the pane, since its dialog may still be on it. Elements have the same fields as permission_requests'. While it is not empty, plain send-keys without expect_pane_sha256, and pause, are refused. Always a non-null array. It follows the row's live state: with [state] settle_ms set, a row can read ended or missing with requests here for up to settle_ms.
- `transcript_status` (string): Derived operator-facing summary of the current session's transcript state: 'present' (jsonl_path recorded), 'never_written' (session id but NULL jsonl_path and prior_sessions is empty — nothing was ever written in the current life), 'rotated' (NULL jsonl_path but prior_sessions is non-empty — the current life has history under a different session id), or 'no_session' (no session_id yet). Session history belongs to a life; 'never_written' and 'rotated' are decided on the same entries prior_sessions lists. Same-agent reuse retains the history; an agent switch or switch back starts a new life with no history. A failed reuse's applied restore returns the pre-reuse life.
- `prior_sessions` ([]object): Archived prior sessions of the current life, newest first, excluding the row's current session id. Same-agent reuse retains session history; an agent switch or switch back starts a new life, hiding earlier lives. Resume continues only the current session; older sessions are listed for inspection only. A failed reuse's applied restore returns the pre-reuse life's history. Always a non-null array ([] when empty). Each element: session_id (string) — archived session id; jsonl_path (string) — archived transcript path (may be empty); recorded_at (timestamp) — when the archive was written (the rotation moment).

### Errors

- `ErrSpawnNotFound`

## send-keys

Strip `\r`, keep `\n`, add Enter (empty text: Enter only). request_token: one key. Native: readiness, 512-byte UTF-8 chunks/drain, one Enter, exact proof; else pane input. ErrSubmissionUnconfirmed: no auto-retry text/Enter; see hook-derived get/status, escalate if unknown. ErrTmuxSendKeys (GONE: the row's session is not there), ErrTmuxUnresponsive (UNAVAILABLE), ErrTmuxSessionConflict (CONFLICT), ErrTmuxNotAvailable (ENVIRONMENT). Unusable recorded name: ErrInternal (see kill).

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the live Spawn to drive.
- `text` (string, optional): Text to type into the Spawn's input. `\r` stripped pre-send; `\n` preserved as newline-in-input. Empty/omitted: nothing typed (Enter only, unless no_enter or key). Exclusive with key; must be empty on a pane answer.
- `delivery_request_id` (string, optional): Owns one native ordinary text attempt on this launch (1-128 letters, digits, underscore or hyphen). Retry the same id and normalized text to observe without replay, after state, relay and dialog guards pass. A fresh id permits an intentional identical native turn. Omitted ids conservatively reuse the last confirmed identical native payload. Existing unresolved native input blocks fallback resends too. Fallback pane input has no native request deduplication guarantee. Exclusive with manual key, no_enter, pane hash and permission answers.
- `allow_pending` (bool, optional): When true, also allows a pending row: a launch (spawn, reuse or resume) whose agent has not reported in yet. Keys are delivered only to a session started by the row's current launch. ended and missing rows are still rejected (ErrSpawnNotInteractive), including requests to reconcile stored or late proof.
- `no_enter` (bool, optional): Type text with no Enter after it. With neither text nor key: ErrInvalidFlags (nothing to send). A pane answer never presses Enter.
- `key` (string, optional): Send this one key instead of text, never followed by Enter: a named key (Escape, Enter, Up, Down, Tab), sent by name, or one character, typed literally. The caller picks the key; agent-director never interprets the screen. Required on a pane answer. Anything else: ErrInvalidFlags.
- `expect_pane_sha256` (string, optional): Required on a pane answer, optional otherwise. The pane_sha256 read-pane returned for the pane the caller looked at (64 hex digits). Before acting, the agent's pane is captured with the same n_lines, ANSI stripped as read-pane gives it by default, and its SHA-256 compared byte for byte; a difference is ErrPaneChanged, nothing done, and the error does not carry the new hash: read the pane again. It means a person or LLM judged this exact screen: never pass it from an automatic flow. On a plain call a matching hash also passes the hold of a request not proven gone (ErrDialogMaybeOpen); every other refusal still applies.
- `n_lines` (int, optional): The n_lines of the read-pane expect_pane_sha256 came from. Defaults to 25 when 0/omitted.
- `request_token` (string, optional): Makes the call a pane answer to this permission request of the Spawn (as get, get-permission or ErrRelayFallenBack's err_details name it): with as, key and expect_pane_sha256, and no text, it sends exactly one key and never Enter. Accepted only once the request has fallen back (its relay hook gone, no verdict acked, no pane answer completed), while no relay hook of the Spawn may still answer (else ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed) and no other pane answer on it is still being sent (else ErrPaneAnswerInProgress). pane_answer intent means sending started but whether the key was sent is unknown; sent records the key was sent, with decision as and decision_reason pane, not ACP delivery, agent receipt or proof. Not open: ErrNoOpenPermissionRequest or ErrAlreadyDecided. A retry after a sender that died is accepted with a fresh hash. Without it the call is plain: refused with ErrRelayFallenBack (with err_details) while any request of the Spawn has fallen back with no pane answer recorded, then, without expect_pane_sha256, with ErrDialogMaybeOpen (with err_details) while any request of the Spawn is not proven gone by the agent (get's unproven_requests), whatever agent-director's records say of it.
- `as` (string, optional): A pane answer's claimed verdict, allow or deny: recorded as the request's pane_as and, once its key is sent, its decision. The public send-keys operation stores the claim without screen verification or proof. Before answering ACP, Cursor additionally requires the sent claim to match the actual selected offered option's verdict. Only with request_token.

### Result

- `request_id` (string): Native ordinary delivery attempt identity; absent on fallback pane input and manual operations.
- `outcome` (string): submitted only with exact native transcript proof; absent on fallback pane input and manual operations.
- `session_id` (string): Native session that recorded the ordinary prompt.
- `record_id` (string): Native user record id when provided by the pinned schema.
- `record_sha256` (string): SHA-256 of the exact structured user record.

### Errors

- `ErrInvalidFlags`
- `ErrSpawnNotFound`
- `ErrSpawnNotInteractive`
- `ErrSubmissionUnconfirmed`
- `ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed`
- `ErrRelayFallenBack`
- `ErrDialogMaybeOpen`
- `ErrNoOpenPermissionRequest`
- `ErrAlreadyDecided`
- `ErrPaneAnswerInProgress`
- `ErrPaneChanged`
- `ErrStoreBusy`
- `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`
- `ErrTmuxSendKeys`
- `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`
- `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`

## read-pane

Capture the last N lines of the agent's own pane (default 25, no upper cap). ANSI escapes stripped, unicode glyphs kept, unless `ansi=true` (raw bytes). tmux errors: ErrTmuxCaptureFailed (GONE: only it means the row's session is not there), ErrTmuxUnresponsive (UNAVAILABLE), ErrTmuxSessionConflict (CONFLICT), ErrTmuxNotAvailable (ENVIRONMENT). Unusable recorded name: ErrInternal (see kill).

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the Spawn to read.
- `n_lines` (int, optional): Number of trailing pane lines to return. Defaults to 25 when 0/omitted. No upper cap. A negative value is refused (ErrInvalidFlags).
- `ansi` (bool, optional): When true, return raw bytes from tmux (escape codes preserved). When false (default), strip ANSI sequences while preserving unicode glyphs.
- `allow_pending` (bool, optional): No effect: pending, ended and missing rows are all readable.

### Result

- `pane` (string): Captured pane text. ANSI handling depends on the `ansi` parameter.
- `pane_sha256` (string): SHA-256, lowercase hex, of exactly the bytes of pane. Pass it as send-keys' or record-pane-answer's expect_pane_sha256, with the same n_lines, when acting on what this pane shows; they compare it with the pane captured as read-pane gives it by default (ANSI stripped), so the hash of an ansi=true read never matches. A checksum: agent-director does not look at what the bytes say.

### Errors

- `ErrInvalidFlags`
- `ErrSpawnNotFound`
- `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`
- `ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`
- `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`
- `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`

## kill

End the agent of a live row's current launch (pending included). kill finds the session with that launch's label on the row's recorded socket, ends the agent's pane and that session by tmux id, and succeeds only once the agent process and every other process found in the session's panes are gone; otherwise it returns ErrTmuxKillFailed. kill_sent says whether a kill was sent. With no session of the launch found, an agent process gone or not recorded is success, nothing sent; one running in another session's pane has that pane ended and is checked again. On a finished row (ended or missing) kill is a no-op success with kill_sent false and no tmux call. `missing` is not proof of exit (see find-missing). kill never changes the row's state: find-missing marks it once its agent process is gone. kill never signals a process itself; one the agent started can outlive a successful kill. On a pending row, before the launch created its session, kill returns kill_sent false and does not stop the launch. kill never ends an earlier launch's session. Success is judged per call: if ErrTmuxKillFailed named a non-agent process outliving the kill, later calls do not track it: a retried kill checks only the agent process. A retry's success means only that the agent is gone; the named process needs a human (see docs/operator-actions.md). If the row finishes while kill waits and the agent outlives the wait, kill returns ErrTmuxKillFailed; a retried kill is a finished-row no-op. Errors (for kill, GONE is success): ErrTmuxKillFailed (UNAVAILABLE): after a kill the agent process or another process of the session's panes ran past the kill exit wait, or the process cannot be checked and its labelled session remains, or no session or pane of this launch was found while the agent process runs; retry later. ErrTmuxUnresponsive (UNAVAILABLE): tmux did not answer usably, before or after a kill was sent; retry later with backoff. ErrTmuxSessionConflict (CONFLICT, permanent until a human looks): the session found is not this launch's, or tmux holds conflicting labels; no kill was sent (see docs/operator-actions.md). ErrTmuxNotAvailable (ENVIRONMENT): tmux could not be run, its socket is not accessible to this user, or this is not the agent's tmux server; an operator must fix it. A repeated kill right after the last session on its tmux server ends can get ErrTmuxUnresponsive or ErrTmuxNotAvailable while the server exits; the caller waits and checks again. ErrSpawnNotFound: no row has this id. None of these errors means that the agent is dead. kill must run as the same user and in the same tmux environment as the agents. So kill's success on a finished row is not verification of exit; on the wrong tmux server, a row wrongly marked missing, kill's no-op success and a reuse together start a second agent for the same id. Agents never run expire (operator-scheduled finished-row cleanup). A live row whose recorded tmux session name cannot be used (empty, or containing a control character or a character tmux stores differently) gets ErrInternal with no tmux call; removing the row is a human's decision (see docs/operator-actions.md). Live-row sequence (a pending row included): 1. kill and check the result; on an error follow its class. 2. If pending, wait until its launch start (status) plus the pending grace period (60 s unless configured); inside it, wait and check again, never escalate. 3. Run find-missing, then check status; repeat about 5 s apart until ended or missing, at most three runs. 4. Still live: kill once more, wait about 5 s, run find-missing once more and check. 5. Still live: escalate to a human. 6. Then resume the row if it has a session id and the caller wants the conversation back; otherwise spawn with reuse_finished (--reuse-finished on the CLI) and the row's agent, which get shows; callers whose ids agent-director mints spawn fresh.

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the Spawn to kill.

### Result

- `kill_sent` (bool): True exactly when a pane kill or a session kill was sent, including one whose call failed; false when no kill was sent, for example for a finished row.

### Errors

- `ErrSpawnNotFound`
- `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`
- `ErrTmuxKillFailed`
- `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`
- `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`

## decide

Caller's allow/deny on open PermissionRequest (relay_mode=on only): first wins (else ErrAlreadyDecided). Cursor allow: offered allow_once or blocking-plan acceptance; deny: supported rejection; persistent native choices need deliberate pane selection. Up to 1 s for relay-hook ack: delivery delivered/not_confirmed (poll get-permission; ends by confirm_by). Hook gone: immediate ErrRelayFallenBack. ErrNoOpenPermissionRequest (no open token, spawn ended/missing, or dialog may have closed): no pane answer. max_wait_ms blocks required pre-record wait: ErrStoreBusy.

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the Spawn sitting on the PermissionRequest.
- `request_token` (string, required): UUIDv4 token identifying the specific permission request to decide. Required to select one request when the Spawn has several.
- `decision` (string, required): Either `allow` or `deny`.
- `reason` (string, optional): Accepted but ignored; a deny records decision_reason operator regardless of this value.
- `max_wait_ms` (int, optional): Optional bound on the whole call, in milliseconds from its start (no default). Required waits before recording, for the store or a request with no recorded settle instant, respect the bound; if they cannot finish in time, ErrStoreBusy records nothing and a retry is safe. With no time left, recording proceeds only if the store is free at once. The wait for the relay hook's ack also ends at the bound, with not_confirmed: once the verdict is recorded decide never returns ErrStoreBusy. A caller with a deadline passes at most its deadline minus 1 s. Omitted: no bound, the store's busy timeout applies. Negative: ErrInvalidFlags.

### Result

- `delivery` (string): delivered: the relay durably acknowledged the verdict before enqueue/write; this is not agent receipt, execution or dialog closure. not_confirmed: no ack within decide's wait of at most 1 s (or by the max_wait_ms bound); ask get-permission, at the latest at confirm_by, by when it is delivered or fallen_back. decide never returns fallen_back: such a request is refused with ErrRelayFallenBack, or ErrAlreadyDecided once answered at the pane.
- `confirm_by` (timestamp): RFC3339 time by which not_confirmed ends: the relay hook's kill instant plus 2 s, by when its hook has acked (delivered) or is gone (fallen_back). With no recorded settle instant: requested_at plus the relay window plus 2 s. Cursor uses a finite persisted per-request settlement independent of gateway lifetime; relay-off requests settle immediately.
- `hook_alive` (bool?): Whether the request's relay hook process runs, checked in the reader's pid namespace by its pid and start time: true; false (no such process, another start time, or a zombie); null when it cannot be checked (another or unreadable pid namespace, unreadable /proc, or no recorded hook identity). Cursor gateway-local controllers have no hook identity: null, never the gateway PID.
- `hook_gone_at` (timestamp?): When a reader first found the request fallen back; null until then. A reading verb (get, list, get-permission) records it only if the store's write lock is free at that moment, never waiting.
- `attempted_decision` (string?): The verdict a decide refused as fallen back (ErrRelayFallenBack) tried to record, the latest one; null when none. Stored and shown, never acted on.
- `attempted_at` (timestamp?): When that refused decide ran; null when none.
- `tool_use_id` (string?): The hook's tool_use_id or Cursor's supplied toolCallId; null when none was given.
- `pane_answer` (string): How the request was answered at the pane. none: no pane answer recorded through agent-director (something outside it, such as a person at tmux, may still have answered it). intent: a pane answer through send-keys was started and whether its key was typed is unknown. sent: its key was sent or the Cursor gateway recorded its native choice (decision_reason pane); this does not establish ACP delivery, agent receipt or execution. outside: a caller recorded it answered outside agent-director (record-pane-answer, decision_reason pane_outside). tool_ran: the agent's hooks or validated correlated Cursor execution output established its tool ran. The hook close records decision allow and decision_reason tool_ran; Cursor proof preserves any earlier verdict and non-null reason, filling a missing reason with tool_ran. A request with sent, outside or tool_ran is closed and stays delivery fallen_back.
- `pane_as` (string?): The verdict a pane answer claims: allow, deny, or unknown (an outside record that did not see the answer); null when none was recorded. Public send-keys and outside records store a claim without screen verification or proof. Before answering ACP, Cursor additionally requires a sent claim to match the actual selected option verdict; an outside record never authorizes an ACP answer.
- `proven_gone_at` (timestamp?): When the agent proved the request's permission dialog gone; null until then. agent-director's own records (delivered, a pane answer, record-pane-answer) are not proof. While it is null, plain send-keys to the live spawn without expect_pane_sha256, and pause, are refused (ErrDialogMaybeOpen).
- `proven_gone_how` (string?): How it was proven gone. tool_ran: a Claude PostToolUse or PostToolUseFailure carried its tool_use_id, or validated correlated Cursor execution output established that exact tool ran (never on a Codex row). turn_end: the turn of the agent that asked ended after it was written; the main agent's Stop or idle-prompt Notification, a Codex main agent's Interrupt (Esc), or a verified Cursor main Stop/Interrupt proves only a durably main-turn-eligible request recorded before the hook began. Legacy non-Cursor main requests retain eligibility; Cursor unknown-origin and child requests are ineligible even without a child id. Decisions, delivery acknowledgements and pane-answer claims do not grant eligibility. agent_gone: its spawn was marked missing, ended or resumed. Null until proven.
- `unproven_since` (timestamp?): For a request not proven gone that no longer awaits an answer in agent-director's records: when its record stopped awaiting one (its relay hook's ack, its pane answer's or record-pane-answer's write, or the close of its spawn's requests; a request with no recorded settle instant: its recorded verdict). Null while it still awaits an answer, and once proven gone.

### Errors

- `ErrMissingRequestToken`
- `ErrSpawnNotFound`
- `ErrRelayModeOff`
- `ErrRelayFallenBack`
- `ErrNoOpenPermissionRequest`
- `ErrAlreadyDecided`
- `ErrAmbiguousRequest`
- `ErrInvalidDecision`
- `ErrInvalidFlags`
- `ErrStoreBusy`

## get-permission

Get by request_token. Cursor: full raw permission/plan params envelope, preserving options/absent/null fields, no added connection context. Undecided: decision/decided_at null. Decided may stay open until acked. Outcome: delivery.

### Parameters

- `request_token` (string, required): UUIDv4 token identifying the permission_requests row to fetch.

### Result

- `request_token` (string): UUIDv4 token the row is keyed under (echoed back).
- `request_id` (int): Autoincrement primary key of the permission_requests row.
- `tool_name` (string): The supplied tool name (e.g. "Bash", "Write") or Cursor action title/plan name.
- `tool_input` (string): Raw JSON string, NOT a nested JSON object; consumers parse it themselves. Cursor preserves the complete received permission/plan params envelope byte for byte, including options and absent/null fields, without adding internal context.
- `requested_at` (timestamp): RFC3339 timestamp when the request was recorded.
- `decision` (string?): "allow" or "deny" once a verdict is recorded; null while undecided, and for a record-pane-answer claiming unknown. A recorded verdict is not the outcome: read delivery and pane_answer.
- `decision_reason` (string?): Canonical decision-reason string: for deny rows operator / timeout / find_missing / ended (find_missing and ended: the request was still undecided when find-missing marked its spawn missing, or when its spawn ended or was resumed, and is closed); pane (a pane answer through send-keys or a Cursor native choice) and pane_outside (record-pane-answer) describe claims, not ACP delivery, receipt or execution proof. tool_ran records tool execution evidence. Initially null while undecided without an outside claim, and for an allow from decide. Validated Cursor execution proof fills a missing reason with tool_ran while preserving any earlier verdict and non-null reason.
- `decided_at` (timestamp?): RFC3339 timestamp when the verdict was written; null while undecided.
- `delivery` (string): delivered: the relay durably acknowledged a verdict before enqueue/write; this is not agent receipt, execution or dialog closure. not_confirmed: no ack yet and the hook may still run; it ends by confirm_by. fallen_back: no ack, and the hook is gone (or cannot be checked and confirm_by has passed): no answer from the relay reached the agent. While pane_answer is none or intent the request awaits an answer unless acknowledged or closed with its spawn; a pane answer, record-pane-answer or validated execution proof can close it; with sent, outside or tool_ran it is closed. Derived on every read; a request with no recorded settle instant falls back by its relay window plus 2 s.
- `confirm_by` (timestamp): RFC3339 time by which not_confirmed ends: the relay hook's kill instant plus 2 s, by when its hook has acked (delivered) or is gone (fallen_back). With no recorded settle instant: requested_at plus the relay window plus 2 s. Cursor uses a finite persisted per-request settlement independent of gateway lifetime; relay-off requests settle immediately.
- `hook_alive` (bool?): Whether the request's relay hook process runs, checked in the reader's pid namespace by its pid and start time: true; false (no such process, another start time, or a zombie); null when it cannot be checked (another or unreadable pid namespace, unreadable /proc, or no recorded hook identity). Cursor gateway-local controllers have no hook identity: null, never the gateway PID.
- `hook_gone_at` (timestamp?): When a reader first found the request fallen back; null until then. A reading verb (get, list, get-permission) records it only if the store's write lock is free at that moment, never waiting.
- `attempted_decision` (string?): The verdict a decide refused as fallen back (ErrRelayFallenBack) tried to record, the latest one; null when none. Stored and shown, never acted on.
- `attempted_at` (timestamp?): When that refused decide ran; null when none.
- `tool_use_id` (string?): The hook's tool_use_id or Cursor's supplied toolCallId; null when none was given.
- `pane_answer` (string): How the request was answered at the pane. none: no pane answer recorded through agent-director (something outside it, such as a person at tmux, may still have answered it). intent: a pane answer through send-keys was started and whether its key was typed is unknown. sent: its key was sent or the Cursor gateway recorded its native choice (decision_reason pane); this does not establish ACP delivery, agent receipt or execution. outside: a caller recorded it answered outside agent-director (record-pane-answer, decision_reason pane_outside). tool_ran: the agent's hooks or validated correlated Cursor execution output established its tool ran. The hook close records decision allow and decision_reason tool_ran; Cursor proof preserves any earlier verdict and non-null reason, filling a missing reason with tool_ran. A request with sent, outside or tool_ran is closed and stays delivery fallen_back.
- `pane_as` (string?): The verdict a pane answer claims: allow, deny, or unknown (an outside record that did not see the answer); null when none was recorded. Public send-keys and outside records store a claim without screen verification or proof. Before answering ACP, Cursor additionally requires a sent claim to match the actual selected option verdict; an outside record never authorizes an ACP answer.
- `proven_gone_at` (timestamp?): When the agent proved the request's permission dialog gone; null until then. agent-director's own records (delivered, a pane answer, record-pane-answer) are not proof. While it is null, plain send-keys to the live spawn without expect_pane_sha256, and pause, are refused (ErrDialogMaybeOpen).
- `proven_gone_how` (string?): How it was proven gone. tool_ran: a Claude PostToolUse or PostToolUseFailure carried its tool_use_id, or validated correlated Cursor execution output established that exact tool ran (never on a Codex row). turn_end: the turn of the agent that asked ended after it was written; the main agent's Stop or idle-prompt Notification, a Codex main agent's Interrupt (Esc), or a verified Cursor main Stop/Interrupt proves only a durably main-turn-eligible request recorded before the hook began. Legacy non-Cursor main requests retain eligibility; Cursor unknown-origin and child requests are ineligible even without a child id. Decisions, delivery acknowledgements and pane-answer claims do not grant eligibility. agent_gone: its spawn was marked missing, ended or resumed. Null until proven.
- `unproven_since` (timestamp?): For a request not proven gone that no longer awaits an answer in agent-director's records: when its record stopped awaiting one (its relay hook's ack, its pane answer's or record-pane-answer's write, or the close of its spawn's requests; a request with no recorded settle instant: its recorded verdict). Null while it still awaits an answer, and once proven gone.

### Errors

- `ErrPermissionRequestNotFound`

## record-pane-answer

Close a fallen-back request answered outside agent-director; types nothing. Needs read-pane's pane_sha256; too soon: ErrClaimTooSoon.

### Parameters

- `request_token` (string, required): Token of the permission request answered outside agent-director (as get, get-permission or ErrRelayFallenBack's err_details name it). Accepted only while it has fallen back (its relay hook gone, no verdict acked, no pane answer completed) and no pane answer through send-keys on it is still being sent (else ErrPaneAnswerInProgress); acked or answered at the pane: ErrAlreadyDecided; closed with its spawn: ErrNoOpenPermissionRequest. Its relay hook must have been gone at least 2 s, from the request's hook_gone_at (written now when it has none), or from its confirm_by when earlier and the hook is judged by time (it cannot be checked, or the request has no recorded settle instant): the agent draws a dialog only after the hook ends, so a pane read sooner may not show it yet; else ErrClaimTooSoon with err_details.not_before (null only while the hook is seen running). Once recorded, plain send-keys is no longer refused with ErrRelayFallenBack on its account; without expect_pane_sha256 it is still refused with ErrDialogMaybeOpen until the agent proves the request gone (its proven_gone_at).
- `as` (string, required): How it was answered, as the caller claims: allow, deny, or unknown. Pass unknown unless the answer was seen. Recorded as pane_as, and as decision (null for unknown) with decision_reason pane_outside; never checked and never authorizes a Cursor ACP answer or supplies proof.
- `expect_pane_sha256` (string, required): Required. The pane_sha256 read-pane returned for the pane the caller looked at (64 hex digits). Before acting, the agent's pane is captured with the same n_lines, ANSI stripped as read-pane gives it by default, and its SHA-256 compared byte for byte; a difference is ErrPaneChanged, nothing done, and the error does not carry the new hash: read the pane again. It means a person or LLM judged this exact screen: never pass it from an automatic flow.
- `n_lines` (int, optional): The n_lines of the read-pane expect_pane_sha256 came from. Defaults to 25 when 0/omitted.

### Result

- `request_token` (string): The request's token (echoed back).
- `pane_answer` (string): Always outside: the request is closed as answered outside agent-director.
- `pane_as` (string): The claim recorded.
- `decision` (string?): The claim when allow or deny; null for unknown.
- `decision_reason` (string): Always pane_outside.

### Errors

- `ErrInvalidFlags`
- `ErrPermissionRequestNotFound`
- `ErrSpawnNotFound`
- `ErrNoOpenPermissionRequest`
- `ErrAlreadyDecided`
- `ErrClaimTooSoon`
- `ErrPaneAnswerInProgress`
- `ErrPaneChanged`
- `ErrStoreBusy`
- `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`
- `ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`
- `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`
- `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`

## resume

Resume latest ended/missing: saved args/env/cwd/transcript; new tmux. Cursor: current cursor_path, latest conversation/protected transcript; native-history loss fails async, no fallback. Replay: saved initial prompt once/launch; no transient input/readiness/decisions/proof. `missing` is not proof of exit (see find-missing). Cwd best-effort pre-trust unless the row's latest spawn set no_pre_trust; pre-trust failure never fails the resume. Returns the instance_id and pre_trust (ok, skipped or failed). Moves the row to pending, keeping its session id and history; parent_id=caller's AGENT_DIRECTOR_INSTANCE_ID; stays pending until the agent reports in, then waiting (Cursor: first verified prompt). Non-timeout failure restores the row's prior ended or missing state; restore failure reported. ErrTmuxNotAvailable ENVIRONMENT; ErrTmuxSessionCreate LAUNCH FAILURE. Create timeout: ErrTmuxUnresponsive (UNAVAILABLE, transient); the session may have been created and the row stays pending; do not retry until get shows the row ended or missing. Pre-move: untouched/retryable. ErrTmuxSessionConflict (CONFLICT, human) or ErrTmuxUnresponsive (starting/stopping): untouched. Held create: restore/refuse. A pending row (a launch in progress): ErrSpawnNotResumable. Cursor: keep row/session/transcript/artifacts. Fresh: kill's live-row advice; unresolved survivors: STOP, human: docs/operator-actions.md#inspect-and-end-a-session-by-hand; spawn agent=cursor, project cwd, omit instance_id, same HOME, known supported extra_env/template intent. None: intended personal login/no custom dirs; dirs don't isolate accounts. Unavailable intent/needs protected data: STOP, human; no saved-env edit/drop credential intent. Saved credential/bad-dir: ErrReservedEnvKey pre-mutation. ErrInternal: control-character id/unusable recorded name (see kill); record failure, no tmux/launch.

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the finished (ended or missing) row to resume. Replay removes parsed session selectors, Claude print mode and cloud controls orphaned by selector removal without changing stored agent_args. Claude inputs missing a recognized required value get literal filtering only; otherwise arguments and option-owned values retain parsed meaning. Claude prompts move behind surviving options and --, and altered short clusters are re-encoded, only when needed to preserve that meaning; otherwise order and spelling survive.

### Result

- `instance_id` (string): The same id passed in (resume keeps the instance id).
- `pre_trust` (string): What the launch's folder-trust pre-trust did. Cursor grants no trust: failed by default, skipped with no_pre_trust. ok = the folder trust took effect (claude: the entry was written to .claude.json; codex: the launch carries the folder trust and the hook-trust bypass); skipped = pre-trust was off for this launch because the row's latest spawn turned it off with no_pre_trust, so nothing was attempted; failed = pre-trust was attempted and the entry was not written (for a claude agent, the .claude.json file is missing, or could not be read, parsed or written, or the row's extra_env sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to a path that is not absolute; for a codex agent, the row's extra_env sets CODEX_HOME to a path that is not absolute, and the launch carries neither the folder trust nor the hook-trust bypass); the launch still proceeds and the agent may stop at its folder-trust prompt (Claude Code's or Codex's).

### Errors

- `ErrSpawnNotFound`
- `ErrSpawnNotResumable`
- `ErrNoSessionId`
- `ErrReservedEnvKey`
- `ErrJsonlMissing`
- `ErrJsonlNeverWritten`
- `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`
- `ErrTmuxSessionCreate`
- `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`
- `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`

## find-missing

Reconcile live rows with their agents. A row's liveness comes only from its agent process, checked by its recorded start time; no process environment is read; no child process or copy of the row's id keeps it alive. A dead agent process marks the row `missing` (a Codex row with an end report: `ended`, not in ids) whatever tmux shows, with no tmux call. Only a row whose process cannot be checked or was never recorded is looked up in tmux, once per socket, on its recorded socket (else the caller's): its own labelled session leaves it unverified (a row with no recorded pane is judged by the pane carrying its launch token, marked if none does), as does an unusable tmux answer; no session of its current launch marks it `missing` whatever holds its name. A session holding the name is never touched (see docs/operator-actions.md). tmux problems never fail the sweep. `missing` is the sweep's judgement on the evidence available to it, not proof that the agent has exited. Run it as the same user and in the same tmux environment as the agents: a run as another user, as root or against another tmux server can mark live rows `missing`. See kill for what a wrong server leads to. Agents never run expire (operator-scheduled finished-row cleanup). ErrProbeUnsupported is no longer returned. A pending row (a spawn's, reuse's or resume's launch) is not judged inside the pending grace period (pending_grace_seconds, 60 s by default), measured from its launch start, not its started_at, or while its launch runs: it is in neither list; one with no readable launch start is judged at once. Past its grace, a pending row whose agent runs but no hook reported gets liveness_note unreported: read-pane, and only having looked, send-keys with allow_pending. To end a live row (pending included) and relaunch its id, follow the live-row sequence in kill's description.

### Parameters

_None._

### Result

- `count` (int): Number of rows this sweep marked `missing` (the length of ids); a Codex row it moved to `ended` is not counted. Zero is a legitimate happy-path result when nothing needed marking.
- `ids` ([]string): Sorted IDs of rows this sweep marked `missing`, on process or tmux evidence: rows whose agent process (the SessionStart one or the recorded pane's) is dead, and rows whose process could not be checked and tmux found no session or pane of their current launch; a pending row only past the pending grace period, and never while the spawn, reuse or resume that began its launch still runs. A row whose guarded write found it changed or gone, or failed, is in neither list, and so is a Codex row the sweep moved to `ended` (its agent process gone and an end report held) and a pending row the sweep notes unreported (its agent alive) or finds already noted so. `missing` is the sweep's judgement on the evidence available to it, not proof that the agent has exited. Never null; [] when none.
- `unverified` (int): Number of live rows this sweep left unverified (the length of unverified_ids).
- `unverified_ids` ([]string): Sorted IDs of live rows this sweep left unverified with a liveness note, whether it wrote the note or found it already current: rows whose agent process could not be checked and which tmux did not mark, for example because their own session is present, tmux could not tell or was unavailable, or tmux was not called, or their recorded tmux session name cannot be used (empty, a control character, or a character tmux stores differently: no tmux call, and a liveness note of its own; removing such a row is a human's decision, see docs/operator-actions.md). Never a pending row inside the pending grace period or while its launch runs. A row whose guarded write found it changed or gone, or failed, a row whose note was cleared, and a pending row noted unreported (its agent alive, no hook reported since its launch; find it by liveness_note in get or list) are in neither list. Never null; [] when none.

### Errors

- `ErrProbeUnsupported`

## expire

Delete finished rows (ended/missing) whose ended_at is older than the retention window (defaults.expire_retention_days; older_than overrides). It reads tmux to decide, deleting a row only if its agent's recorded process is not seen running and tmux shows no session of the agent. It never kills a session or touches transcripts. `missing` is not proof of exit (see find-missing). Finished rows are removed by an operator-scheduled expire at the default retention, run as the same user and in the same tmux environment as the agents; it keeps and reports rows whose session runs or cannot be checked. Agents never run it, least of all with a zero window. A run as another user, as root or against another tmux server can wrongly delete rows.

### Parameters

- `older_than` (duration, optional): Duration override (e.g. `7d`, `2h`). When omitted, defaults.expire_retention_days from config applies.

### Result

- `count` (int): Number of rows deleted (the length of ids): rows deleted after tmux showed no session of the agent (Gone) and its recorded process was not seen running. Zero is a legitimate result when no row was deleted.
- `ids` ([]string): Sorted IDs of the rows deleted after tmux showed no session of the agent (Gone) and its recorded process was not seen running, each only while the row was unchanged since expire examined it. Never null; [] when none.
- `kept` (int): Number of selected rows kept rather than deleted (the length of kept_ids), for example because the agent's process or a session of the agent (its own, or a leftover of an earlier launch) may still run, tmux could not be checked or answered from a different server, the run's tmux time budget (sweep_budget_seconds) was spent, the row changed after it was examined, or its recorded tmux session name cannot be used (kept on every run, before any other check, with no tmux call).
- `kept_ids` ([]string): Sorted IDs of the selected rows kept rather than deleted, each reported with its reason in the trail (ad.expire.kept). A row whose recorded tmux session name cannot be used (empty, a control character, or a character tmux stores differently) is kept on every run, before any other check, with no tmux call and a reason of its own; removing it is a human's decision (see docs/operator-actions.md). tmux problems and a failed delete of one row never fail the run: the row is kept. A failed read of the selected rows fails the run. A row another caller removed first is in neither list. Never null; [] when none.

### Errors

_None._

## make-template

Save a preset as ~/.config/agent-director/templates/NAME.toml. Per-invocation params (template, instance_id, tmux_session_name, reuse_finished) are refused.

### Parameters

- `name` (string, required): Template name. Must be filename-safe (no path separators, no leading dot, no `..`).
- `cwd` (string, optional): Bake a default cwd into the template. Per-call cwd overrides.
- `agent` (string, optional): Bake the template's agent: claude (Claude Code), codex (Codex) or cursor (Cursor fresh Linux ACP), case-sensitive; empty or absent means none, and no agent key is stored. Another value is refused with ErrTemplateMalformed. A non-empty agent_args needs an agent (ErrTemplateAgentMissing): the arguments belong to it. A codex or cursor template with any allow, deny or ask entry is refused with ErrPermissionsUnsupported. A spawn that names no agent takes the template's.
- `relay_mode` (string, optional): Bake a default relay_mode (on/off). Per-call relay_mode (--relay-mode on the CLI) overrides.
- `agent_args` ([]string, optional): Bake default agent argv. Per-call agent_args (on the CLI, spawn's arguments after --) REPLACES the template's array wholesale (not concat). Cursor uses spawn's supported model/mode/initial-prompt subset; unsupported or malformed arguments return ErrSpawnDeniedFlag before writing.
- `extra_env` (map[string]string, optional): Bake env-var entries. Per-call extra_env (--extra-env on the CLI) merges by key; per-call wins on collision. A key spawn would refuse is refused here by the same check with ErrReservedEnvKey, never rewritten, and no file is written: the reserved names AGENT_DIRECTOR_* and HOME with any value (set an absolute CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (Claude Code) or CODEX_HOME (Codex) to give the agent its own config), and a key that is not a valid env-var name (empty, or containing '=' or a NUL byte; the message says which). Cursor templates additionally refuse explicit CURSOR_API_KEY or AGENT_CLI_CREDENTIAL_STORE, even empty, and require nonempty absolute, lexically clean CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR/CURSOR_DATA_DIR paths without control bytes. These directories select configuration/data with existing personal login, without account isolation. Agent-independent templates defer Cursor checks until the effective agent is resolved.
- `label` ([]string, optional): Bake label k=v entries. Per-call label merges by key; per-call wins on collision.
- `allow` ([]string, optional): Bake permissions.allow entries. Per-call allow CONCATENATES (does not replace).
- `deny` ([]string, optional): Bake permissions.deny entries. Per-call deny CONCATENATES.
- `ask` ([]string, optional): Bake permissions.ask entries. Per-call ask CONCATENATES.
- `overwrite` (bool, optional): Replace any existing template at this name atomically. Default false refuses an existing template.

### Result

- `path` (string): Absolute path of the written template file.

### Errors

- `ErrTemplateNameUnsafe`
- `ErrTemplateExists`
- `ErrTemplateMalformed`
- `ErrTemplateAgentMissing`
- `ErrSpawnDeniedFlag`
- `ErrPermissionsUnsupported`
- `ErrReservedEnvKey`

## list

Enumerate rows. All filters AND together. Unordered; callers sort.

### Parameters

- `state` ([]string, optional): Filter by state. Multiple values OR together. Comma-separated on CLI; JSON array via MCP. The filter matches the displayed state, including `stuck`, and is applied before limit.
- `label` ([]string, optional): Filter by label k=v. Repeatable on CLI; each entry must contain a literal `=`. Multiple entries AND together.
- `parent` (string, optional): Filter by parent_id exact match.
- `cwd` (string, optional): Filter by canonicalized cwd exact match.
- `tmux_session_name` (string, optional): Filter by tmux session name exact match. Returns any live or ended row whose tmux_session_name equals the value byte-for-byte; correlation across re-uses, not uniqueness enforcement. Over MCP, a serve process from before the fix (0.10.x and earlier, or 0.11.0-rc.1, which counts as 0.11.0) silently ignores this parameter under either spelling, so list is not filtered by session name.
- `limit` (int, optional): Cap result count. 0 / omitted means no cap. A negative value is refused (ErrInvalidFlags).

### Result

- `spawns` ([]Spawn): Matching rows. Displayed state filtering occurs before limit. Rows displayed stuck carry only stuck_reason, with since/request_token/tool_name omitted. stuck with stuck_reason permission_unanswered reports a current unanswered, unproven fallen-back request on Claude, Codex or Cursor after [state] permission_unanswered_timeout_seconds (whole seconds, default/zero 30, range 1 to 9223372036), measured from its established fallback, followed by ordinary settling detected on reads. Independent requests remain eligible; detail selects earliest fallback, then lexical request token. since is the successful read that committed displayed entry, in RFC3339 UTC with exactly millisecond precision. Clearing retains displayed detail through settlement; representative changes preserve since. Observation writes never wait and skipped samples retain the committed display. This is report-only: raw command guards and dialog holds remain authoritative; live stuck members contribute working to family_state. No background observation is added. Empty array when none match (never null). Each row carries family_state (string: working or waiting). Complete stored family (self and live descendants at every depth, including through retained ended/missing intermediates). Uses stored raw member states: waiting exactly when every live member is waiting, or no live members remain; otherwise working. With [state] settle_ms, both directions settle once from the aggregate change, independently of state and depth. New/upgraded families start raw; later timing survives reopening. List filters and limits do not restrict family membership. Reporting never waits; waiting does not establish readiness, action safety or task success. Permissions remain per agent. Each row carries agent (string: claude, codex or cursor, the agent it runs) and liveness_unverified_since (timestamp?, the time a sweep first noted the row, kept while the note changes) and liveness_note (string?, the latest sweep's reason token, overwritten when the reason changes; or unreported on a pending row whose agent is alive but has not reported through any hook since its launch, kept by a sweep that finds the agent alive and cleared by the agent's next hook: read-pane, and only having looked, send-keys with allow_pending (--allow-pending on the CLI)), both omitted while NULL and cleared together when a sweep finds the agent process alive (except on a pending row noted unreported or provenance_conflict), and launch_started_at (timestamp?), the start of the launch in progress (RFC3339 UTC with millisecond precision), omitted unless the row is pending. It follows the row's live state: with [state] settle_ms set, a row whose agent has reported in can read pending without it for up to settle_ms. Each row's state takes the same values as status, with the same meaning of pending: a launch (spawn, reuse or resume) in progress whose agent has not reported in yet; a resumed pending row keeps its session id and history. `missing` is the sweep's judgement on the evidence available to it, not proof that the agent has exited. With [state] settle_ms set in config.toml (whole milliseconds from 0 to 60000, 0 or unset is off; a value outside that range is refused, never capped), state is the settled state: a state a hook wrote shows only once it has held that long, and the last settled state shows meanwhile, so a change that reverts sooner never shows; ended, missing and a state a command wrote (spawn, resume, find-missing) show at once. Nothing marks a state as late, and the setting covers every caller on the host. A turn shorter than settle_ms never shows (a waiting agent that replies sooner reads waiting throughout), so keep it at 1000 to 2000. Except for independently settled family_state, the row's other fields, and the verbs that act on it (send-keys, decide, pause, resume, kill, find-missing, expire, spawn), follow its live state, which can be newer: a refusal can name a state status does not show yet. Each row also carries permission_requests, as get's: Open permission requests: those that still await an answer (not acked by their relay hook and not answered at the pane, decided or not; a request with no recorded settle instant while undecided). Always a non-null array ([] when empty). Populated only when the row's live state is check_permission; empty array for all other states (a row can read waiting, working or ask_user while a request is still open: follow a tracked request with get-permission). Requests are never delayed by [state] settle_ms, so with it set a row can also read any state (even ended or missing) with open requests listed, or check_permission with [], for up to settle_ms. Each element: request_id (int) — autoincrement row id; request_token (string) — UUIDv4 request token, pass to decide verb to target this row; tool_name (string) — the supplied tool name or Cursor action title/plan name; tool_input (string) — raw JSON string of the tool's input, NOT a nested object (consumers parse it themselves). Cursor preserves the received permission/plan params envelope byte for byte, including options and absent/null fields, without adding internal context; requested_at (RFC3339 timestamp) — when the request was recorded; decision and decision_reason (string?) — the recorded verdict, not the outcome; and the delivery facts as get-permission returns them: delivery (delivered, not_confirmed or fallen_back), confirm_by (timestamp), hook_alive (bool?), hook_gone_at (timestamp?), attempted_decision (string?), attempted_at (timestamp?), tool_use_id (string?), pane_answer (none or intent on an open request), pane_as (string?), proven_gone_at (timestamp?), proven_gone_how (string?) and unproven_since (timestamp?). get and list never wait for the store's write lock.

### Errors

- `ErrInvalidFlags`
- `ErrListInvalidLabel`

## list-subagents

Return an agent's subagent records and whether they are tracked.

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the Spawn whose subagents to list.

### Result

- `tracked` (bool): Whether the row's launch registered subagent tracking: false for a row launched before subagent tracking existed, which has no records, and false for a row whose launch registers no subagent events; true for any other row.
- `subagents` ([]object): Every subagent record of the row's current life, across every launch of it. Empty array when it has none (never null). Ordered by first_started_at ascending (records with a null first_started_at last), then subagent_id. Each element has all of these keys, a field with no known value null: subagent_id (string) — the subagent's id, unique among the records shown for its row; instance_id (string) — the row's id; session_id (string?) — the session of the event that created the record, never changed after; subagent_type (string?) — its type; description (string?) — the short description the launching call gave it, never the prompt text; model (string?) — the model it runs; parent_type (string?) — what launched it: agent (the row's own agent, so parent_id is the row's instance_id) or subagent (another subagent, so parent_id is that subagent's subagent_id); parent_id (string?) — as parent_type says; tool_use_id (string?) — the id of the tool call that launched it; run_mode (string?) — background or foreground; first_started_at (timestamp?) — when it first started; started_at (timestamp?) — when its latest run started; stopped_at (timestamp?) — when it last stopped, null if it never has (kept when it runs again); lost_at (timestamp?) — when it was judged lost, null unless it was; state (string) — running (started, neither stopped nor judged lost), stopped (its agent reported it finished) or lost (judged gone without a stop report); close_reason (string?) — why it is no longer running, null exactly while state is running: stop_event (its agent reported it finished), absent_from_snapshot (a snapshot of the agent's running background tasks did not list it) or agent_gone (its agent ended, went missing or began a new launch). Each timestamp is RFC3339 UTC with millisecond precision (trailing zeros dropped, no fraction on a whole second). context (object) — Experimental context estimate: agent internals and this output shape have no stable-format guarantee. Always an object with used_tokens (integer?), window_tokens (integer?), fraction (number?; used_tokens divided by window_tokens), source (string?) and as_of (RFC3339 UTC timestamp with millisecond precision?). Unknown retains all five keys with null values. Readings estimate last-response occupancy, never cumulative billing. Claude 2.1.280 first-party pairs automatically composed capacity callbacks with on-demand transcript usage for the same resolved model, response and current live writer, without provider, endpoint or window overrides. Codex 0.159.2 OpenAI requires admitted fresh-startup provenance and a current live writer; existing, resumed or unproven sessions return unknown. Its sequential rollouts pair last_token_usage.total_tokens with the same session's reported usable model_context_window; source codex_jsonl_last_token_usage. as_of is the source measurement time, never read time. Claude and Codex usage is read on demand without a usage cache or wall-clock age cutoff; stored capacity metadata is not cached usage. Missing, malformed, incomplete, unsupported or unresolvable evidence yields unknown; compaction requires later valid usage. Both Cursor versions have successful native interactive captures. Managed ACP lacks the ordinary usage-bearing afterAgentResponse/stop path, exposes only stopReason in prompt results and exposes no manual /summarize command. Both versions have a native shared-resource preCompact executor path; automatic managed delivery remains unqualified. Cursor context is unknown in this build; numeric support is deferred until upstream ACP supplies usage. A visible Claude child can qualify with its own capacity metadata and transcript path for the same response; otherwise child context is unknown. Parent usage or capacity is never substituted.

### Errors

- `ErrSpawnNotFound`

## pause

Send `/exit` to a waiting row; await `ended` for pause.timeout_seconds. Ended/missing: no-op. `missing` is not proof of exit (see find-missing). ErrPauseTimeout: inspection_required; inspect get/read-pane before more keys; no blind retries. Codex: once the agent is gone with an end report, ends the row (before the keys or in the wait). Plain send-keys guards; past ErrDialogMaybeOpen: answer any dialog, send-keys `/exit` with expect_pane_sha256; or kill. ErrTmuxSendKeys (GONE: only it means the row's session is not there), ErrTmuxUnresponsive (UNAVAILABLE), ErrTmuxSessionConflict (CONFLICT), ErrTmuxNotAvailable (ENVIRONMENT). Unusable recorded name: ErrInternal (see kill).

### Parameters

- `instance_id` (string, required): Id of the Spawn to pause.

### Result

_None._

### Errors

- `ErrSpawnNotFound`
- `ErrSpawnNotPausable`
- `ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed`
- `ErrRelayFallenBack`
- `ErrDialogMaybeOpen`
- `ErrPauseTimeout`
- `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`
- `ErrTmuxSendKeys`
- `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`
- `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`

## trail-emit

Emit an ad.* trail event (sub-verb relay-attempt) without opening state.db.

### Parameters

- `sub_verb` (string, required): Sub-verb to invoke. Currently: relay-attempt.
- `token` (string, required): request_token. Required.
- `endpoint` (string, required): target_endpoint (URL or socket path). Required.
- `outcome` (string|int, required): 3-digit HTTP status code (100-599, emitted as integer) or named error class: connection_refused, timeout, dns_failure (emitted as string). Required.
- `bytes_sent` (int, optional): Bytes sent. Default 0. A negative value is refused (ErrInvalidFlags).
- `bytes_received` (int, optional): Bytes received. Default 0. A negative value is refused (ErrInvalidFlags).
- `instance_id` (string, required): instance_id. Required.

### Result

_None._

- `ErrInvalidFlags`

## hook

Internal: row's hooks write; others: ad.hook.ignored. Lifecycle: exit 0 (fail-open); Claude context callbacks forward command exit status.

### Parameters

- `stdin` (json, required): Agent hook payload (hook_event_name, transcript_path, tool_name, reason, ...).
- `agent` (string, optional): The agent whose hook this is. Absent: claude. Any other value is a hook failure (fail-open; a relayed PermissionRequest is denied).
- `timeout` (int, optional): The per-hook timeout, in seconds, spawn wrote for this hook in the agent's settings (the PermissionRequest entry: the relay window). The relay hook's kill instant is its start plus it; the hook never acks a verdict without 2 s left before it. Absent, unparseable or not positive: the loaded config's relay.timeout_seconds.
- `context_source` (string, optional): Internal native Claude capacity callback: statusLine or subagentStatusLine, set automatically by spawn. Absent or empty: ordinary lifecycle hook handling.
- `context_forward` (string, optional): Internal original Claude status-line command, encoded as unpadded standard base64 by spawn. Native capacity callbacks preserve its stdin, stdout, stderr and exit status. Absent or empty: no command to forward.

### Result

_None._

### Errors

_None._
